text.p: Italian bond futures started on a firmer trend helped by overnight Treasuries and the early positive trend to German bunds, but European markets were a little cautious ahead of U.S. data later today, dealers said.

After Monday's near one full point rally on BTP futures, dealers expect the market to attempt to consolidate around these level, and watch other European bond markets and the lira for immediate direction.
Weekend local elections were a setback for the centre-left government and strengthened the Communist Refoundation party, on which the government relies for support.

Dealers said that the local elections will do nothing to ease the government's difficulties in pushing through key structural reforms as the elections appear to have strengthened the bargaining power of the Communists.

They added that confidence on Monday from Treasury minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi on Italy meeting EMU targets was tempered by foreign minister Lamberto Dini saying his party's support for Romano Prodi's government coalition was conditional on achieving promised budget consolidation.
Trading likely to be be quiet ahead of the U.S. first quarter employment cost numbers later today, dealers added.
With no strong words to restrain the dollar from the weekend G7 meeting, the dollar continued to be buoyant helping the lira edge towards its 990 lire/mark ERM central parity, dealers said.
